lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The file includes date of birth and nationality, personal details a reader is not meant to weigh.
items.because: They are not relevant to assessing work or qualifications and draw attention away from professional evidence.

items.says: Education appears before Experience, delaying the product internship and operations background.
items.because: A reader encounters the degrees before the work history that establishes the candidate’s direction.

items.says: The eight-month gap between the B.A. and the Operations Analyst role is unexplained.
The 35% checkout-conversion increase does not say whether it is relative or percentage-point growth or what it is compared with.
items.because: Without that anchor, a reader cannot judge the size of the improvement.

items.says: The shipping result is buried after the requirements and stakeholder list.
items.because: A reader reaches the outcome only after the work description and people involved.

items.says: The roadmap-priority outcome is buried, and “the business case that set” is an awkward link.
items.because: The methods and loss estimate come before why the work mattered, and the link to the roadmap decision is indirect.

items.says: Comparing merchants who chose different flows does not isolate the redesign’s effect.
items.because: The groups may differ in ways that affect onboarding outcomes without random assignment or adequate adjustment.

items.says: The bullet gives a comparison method but no result or insight.
items.because: The comparison setup alone does not show whether onboarding improved or what changed.

items.says: The onboarding result is attributed to both Harbor Payments and the earlier practicum.
items.because: The practicum places the same 2,300-merchant result before the Harbor internship began, creating a conflict about the role and timing.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments does not support claiming overall late deliveries fell from 11% to 7%.
items.because: The lower rate could reflect the changed population rather than fewer late deliveries overall.

items.says: The pick-error result should lead the Crestline entry.
items.because: Its quantified reduction, two-site reach and work with supervisors and pickers make it a clear accomplishment.

items.says: “Prepares” uses present tense in a role that ended in August 2023.
items.because: It conflicts with “Coordinated” and makes the forecast-pack work sound ongoing.

items.says: The review and forecast-pack bullet gives no outcome they enabled.
items.because: Without a decision, planning result or other consequence, the contribution’s value is difficult to judge.

items.says: The launch bullet does not name the candidate’s specific product or rollout contribution.
items.because: A reader can see the outcome but not what the product lead owned.

items.says: “That would have been thrown away” repeats the meaning of “surplus food.”
“Launched” repeats the opening verb of the preceding bullet.
“Each week” and “a week” repeat the weekly cadence.
The weekly sessions are described without saying what they produced.
items.because: The cadence and participants do not establish an outcome or the value delivered.

items.says: The intake-form result should lead the practicum entry.
items.because: The work spans four clinics, and front-desk staff adopted the changes.

items.says: The intake-form bullet uses passive voice, obscuring who did the work.
The bullet does not quantify how much the intake form was shortened.
The merchant-onboarding bullet does not fit the hospital practicum and duplicates the Harbor Payments result.
items.because: The entry describes outpatient scheduling, while the bullet describes merchant payments and repeats a result listed under Harbor.

items.says: “By redesigning onboarding” does not identify what changed in the process.
items.because: It names a broad activity rather than the specific change made.

items.says: “Takes” uses present tense for a practicum that ended in May 2024.
items.because: It makes the completed result sound ongoing.
